children: Perma-Pipe reported second quarter fiscal 2026 results with net sales of $59.6 million, up 24.4% year-over-year, and net income attributable to common stock of $2.5 million, or $0.31 per diluted share. Gross profit was $17.4 million (29.2% margin) and adjusted income before tax was $8.3 million for the quarter. The company ended the quarter with $31.8 million in cash and a backlog of $142.3 million supported by over $67 million of Q2 awards.
Revenue: Net sales of $59.6 million for the three months ended July 31, 2026, up 24.4% from $47.9 million in Q2 FY2025.
Gross profit and margin: Gross profit of $17.4 million for the quarter; gross margin 29.2% (prior-year quarter 30.1%).
Operating income: Income from operations of $4.3 million for the quarter versus $3.2 million in the prior-year quarter.
Net income and EPS: Net income attributable to common stock of $2.5 million, or $0.31 per diluted share, compared with $0.10 diluted in Q2 FY2025.
Non-GAAP adjusted: Adjusted income before tax of $8.3 million for the quarter (reconciling adjustments include a $3.9 million non-recurring customer charge and $0.5 million Ohio start-up costs).

Backlog and awards: Backlog increased to $142.3 million at July 31, 2026, from $136.5 million at April 30, 2026, bolstered by more than $67 million of new orders in Q2, including significant oil & gas awards in MENA and Canada and the company's first critical-cooling infrastructure award in MENA.

Facility expansion and production ramp: Commenced operations and ramped production at a new Ohio manufacturing facility to support higher U.S. demand; incurred related start-up costs during the quarter.

MENA and international growth: Expanding the Qatar facility to meet local demand and entered a memorandum of understanding post-quarter to form a joint venture in Jordan to support a government-backed water-security infrastructure program and future cross-border projects.

Working capital and liquidity actions: Operating activities generated approximately $7.2 million of cash in Q2 driven by net income and favorable working capital changes; capital expenditures were about $2.0 million in the quarter.

Capital structure update: Replaced prior asset-based facility with a new global credit agreement providing a $75.0 million revolver and $14.0 million term loan (approximately $90 million committed at closing) and used proceeds to repay prior indebtedness and a mortgage on an Alberta plant.
